problem: Earlier dialog-based embodied benchmarks (CVDN, DialFRED, AVDN, TEACh, RMM) evaluate either task performers that follow human-written dialog, or helper–performer pairs trained and scored jointly. None evaluates a navigation-helper agent on its own, i.e., how useful its natural-language answers to a performer's help requests are. Using humans as performers for this evaluation is costly and slow.
motivation: Helper agents have oracle knowledge (goal location, map) and answer a performer's questions, for example as an accessibility aid. Their quality should be judged by how much they improve the performer's task success, not by text overlap with human answers. The authors observe that a helper whose outputs are less similar to human responses (lower BLEU/ROUGE) can still produce more task progress.
key_idea: Score a helper agent by feeding its responses to a fixed pre-trained performer agent (R2H benchmark with the RDH and RdI tasks on CVDN, DialFRED and AVDN) and measuring the performer's task metric. The paper also builds SeeRee, a video-language response generator with a learnable input-conditioned sparse attention mask (COS), trained on GPT-3-restructured step-by-step responses (Parse by Step).
insight: Helpfulness and linguistic similarity to human helpers diverge. In the CVDN ablation, adding Parse by Step lowers BLEU-2 (14.4→13.8 seen) and ROUGE-L (25.5→24.2 seen) but raises performer GP (5.9→6.5 seen, 4.7→4.9 unseen). Applying Parse by Step to the human validation responses keeps GP (6.9→7.3 seen, 5.1→5.1 unseen), so the restructuring removes noise without losing task information. The COS mask helps GP on seen (5.4→5.9) but not unseen (4.7→4.7). A zero-shot multimodal LLM (mPLUG-Owl) is competitive indoors, collapses on aerial AVDN (SPL 0.7/1.5), and in multi-turn RdI ends best but with noisier per-turn effect than SeeRee.
method: R2H benchmark: helper-only evaluation in which helper responses drive a fixed pre-trained performer. The performer's task metric (GP on CVDN, SR on DialFRED, SPL on AVDN) measures response quality.

RDH task (Respond to Dialog History): the helper's response r̂_i replaces the human answer to inquiry q_i and is appended to the human dialog history h_{i-1}. Performers are HAMT (CVDN), the DialFRED model and HAA-Transformer (AVDN); the latter two were reproduced because weights were unavailable.

RdI task (Respond during Interaction): no initial dialog. The performer (RMM Navigator N + Questioner Q, which asks after every 4 actions) queries the helper repeatedly for up to 20 turns on CVDN, which also measures communication efficiency. DialFRED has one QA per trajectory, so it is excluded from RdI.

Environment-specific oracle samplers: scripts convert each environment into an image sequence of the performer's views along the shortest path to the goal. On CVDN the sequence is limited to 5 viewpoints ahead via the connectivity graph. On AVDN the views are north-up with a red arrow showing drone heading, and a green box marks the destination in the prompts.

SeeRee: image sequence padded to fixed length, encoded by Video Swin Transformer, concatenated with BERT embeddings of the inquiry plus [CLS], and fed to a multimodal transformer initialized from SwinBERT. It is trained with MLM (80% [MSK], 10% random) and decodes responses auto-regressively by filling [MSK] tokens.

COS (Conditional Optimized Sparse) attention mask: inquiry tokens attend to themselves and to visual tokens; response tokens attend causally. Visual-to-visual attention uses a non-binary mask C = sigmoid(MLP(VE)) conditioned on the visual embeddings and regularized by an L1 sparsity loss. This contrasts with SwinBERT's mask, which is fixed after training.

Parse by Step: GPT-3 few-shot prompts rewrite the human training responses into numbered step-by-step instructions (numbers removed afterwards), and SeeRee is trained on these. A second helper is zero-shot mPLUG-Owl, given the image sequence plus a dataset-specific prompt.

setting.backbone: SeeRee: Video Swin Transformer + BERT embeddings + multimodal transformer initialized from SwinBERT (fine-tuned per dataset). Alternative helper: mPLUG-Owl (frozen, zero-shot). Navigation decisions are made by fixed pre-trained performers: HAMT, DialFRED model, HAA-Transformer, RMM N+Q.
setting.training_data: SeeRee is fine-tuned separately on the training sets of CVDN, DialFRED and AVDN, converted into (oracle image sequence, inquiry, response) samples. Responses are rewritten by GPT-3 (Parse by Step). Benchmark stats: 2050 CVDN, 120958 DialFRED and 5372 AVDN navigation trajectories. Training: 20k iterations, batch 6, lr 1e-4, AdamW, about 12 h on one A6000. The mPLUG-Owl helper uses no task training.
setting.observation: Helper: an oracle image sequence of performer views along the shortest path to the goal (CVDN ≤5 viewpoints ahead; AVDN north-up top-down drone views with heading arrow) plus the text inquiry and dialog. Performers use their native observations (e.g., HAMT panoramic RGB).
setting.action_space: Helper outputs free-form natural-language responses. Performers act in native spaces: CVDN nav-graph viewpoints, DialFRED/AI2-THOR discrete actions, AVDN continuous drone waypoints.
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (CVDN), AI2-THOR (DialFRED), AVDN continuous photo-realistic drone simulator
setting.privileged: Helper uses oracle information by design: goal location and shortest-path image sequences sampled from the environment/connectivity graph. Performers get no privileged info.

numbers_note: All numbers are helper-agent scores (the fixed performer's metrics under the helper's responses), not navigator results, so they are not comparable to standard CVDN/DialFRED/AVDN leaderboards. The main RdI result (mean GP vs. number of dialog turns, max 20 turns, CVDN val-unseen, SeeRee vs. mLLM vs. RMM G) is shown only in a figure without numbers. Table 2 (RMM N+Q performer) is captioned as a 'two-agent task built on CVDN' and is not explicitly tied to the RdI protocol in the text. Appendix LLM baselines (mPLUG-Owl + ChatGPT; BLIP2 with stacked images) are omitted here because the paper calls them baselines: BLIP2 gets CVDN GP 5.6/3.4, DialFRED SR 38.6/24.7, AVDN SPL 3.8/5.0 (seen/unseen), so it beats both SeeRee (4.6 seen) and mPLUG-Owl on AVDN val-unseen SPL (5.0 vs 4.4).
results: In RDH, SeeRee gives the best helper performance on nearly all splits and comes close to human helpers indoors: CVDN GP 6.5/4.9 (seen/unseen) vs human 6.9/5.1, RMM Guide 4.7/2.8 and mPLUG-Owl 5.3/3.6; DialFRED SR 49.1/33.1 vs human 49.1/33.4. The zero-shot mLLM is slightly better on DialFRED unseen (33.8). On AVDN every helper stays far below humans: SeeRee SPL 4.6/4.4 vs human 14.7/16.5 vs RMM G 2.4/3.6, and GP is negative for all helpers. With human performers on 60 CVDN episodes, SeeRee gives the highest GP (9.89 vs 8.44 mLLM, 6.32 RMM G, 3.54 no helper) and the highest faithfulness (75/100), but the lowest naturalness (72/100).
limitations: Helper evaluation depends on the capability of the performer agent. The only performer that can both ask and navigate (RMM N+Q, LSTM) is weak, so RdI is run only on CVDN (DialFRED has single-turn dialogs; AVDN has no asking performer).

Helpers rely on oracle shortest-path image sequences, and everything is in simulation. On aerial AVDN, all helpers, including zero-shot mLLMs, are far below human helpers and produce negative goal progress.
Dialog-based embodied datasets are small, and the human evaluation is limited (5 students, 60 trajectories).
